clue.text: Jailbird's back in prison, crazy and condemnatory

parts.note: jug is slang for prison

parts.note: the word whose final letter is taken
mental is informal for crazy

explanation.surface: A prisoner losing his mind behind bars, while someone judges him harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being judgmental means being quick to criticise or condemn others.

clue.text: Court members, when Wimbledon final often held, swapping sides

indicators.note: the sides are left and right, so the L is exchanged for an R

parts.note: the Wimbledon tennis finals are usually played in early July

explanation.surface: Tennis talk: the Wimbledon final with players changing ends, with 'Court' as a tennis court.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis championship. 'Swapping sides' swaps L (left) for R (right) in JULY.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury is the panel of citizens sitting in a law court to decide a verdict.

clue.text: One's banged part of femur driving northwards

indicators.note: northwards says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the letters are found within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An orthopaedic picture: a bone that took a knock in a car crash.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft folded 'part' into the definition, but 'part of' is the signal for letters found inside 'femur driving'; 'One's banged' alone is the drum.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum is an instrument that is struck or beaten, so it is one that gets banged.

clue.text: Having aimed to diversify, Stuart passes college course?

indicators.note: to diversify is to vary, so the letters of aimed are rearranged

parts.note: Stu is the short form of the name Stuart
to pass away is to die, so passes gives dies

explanation.surface: A student called Stuart, having set his sights wider, gets through his college studies.
explanation.walkthrough: AIMED rearranged gives MEDIA; the question mark flags that this is one example of a college course.
explanation.definitionFit: Media studies is an academic subject about newspapers, television and other mass communications, offered by colleges.

clue.text: How's your father? Not bad, getting through that upset

indicators.note: getting through puts the OK inside the reversed word
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: yon is an old or dialect word for that
OK means acceptable, not bad

explanation.surface: A cheery greeting asking after someone's dad, who is apparently doing fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How's your father' is British slang for sex, as is nooky, so the polite question is really the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are humorous British slang for sexual activity, so one stands in for the other.

clue.text: Alliance outwardly Green when getting in fuel

indicators.note: getting in says those outer letters go inside the fuel word

parts.note: aliment is food, the fuel for the body

indicators.note: outwardly takes just the outside letters of the word

parts.note: the word whose first and last letters are used

explanation.surface: Politics and energy: a coalition with the Green party, formed when talking about fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like the political party, but only its outside letters G and N are used, and they go inside ALIMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An alignment is an arrangement of countries or parties in agreement, a synonym for an alliance.

clue.text: State level of intelligence when describing artist

indicators.note: describing in the sense of drawing a line around, so IQ goes round RA

parts.note: IQ is intelligence quotient
RA is Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A report on how intelligent a painter is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describing' is used in its geometric sense of drawing a line around something, the way a compass describes a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraq is a sovereign country in the Middle East, and a state is a nation.

clue.text: Courteous still around training college

indicators.note: around means the calm word goes round the other letters

parts.note: restful means calm and still
PE is physical education, sports training

explanation.surface: Someone who stays polite throughout their time at a training college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb meaning 'nevertheless', but it is the adjective, giving RESTFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Being respectful means showing politeness and regard to others, which is courtesy.

clue.text: Bike hired to trail right up a one in four

indicators.note: to trail means to follow behind, so the hired word comes last

parts.note: a quad is a quad bike, a four-wheeled motorbike
taken as written
let means rented out or hired

explanation.surface: A hired bike being pushed up a steep one-in-four hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One in four' reads like a gradient, but it means one of four babies born together.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadruplet is one of four children born at a single birth.

clue.text: Beat Nick in tournament

parts.note: a police officer's beat is their round
to nick is British slang for steal or rob
taken as written

explanation.surface: A police beat, with an officer nicking someone at a sports event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' is British slang both for steal and arrest; here it means rob.
explanation.definitionFit: A round robin is a competition format in which every player meets every other player in turn.

clue.text: Regular findings of moose and stag bones

indicators.note: regular findings are letters taken at even intervals, every other one

parts.note: the word whose second and fourth letters are taken
the word whose first and third letters are taken

explanation.surface: An archaeologist turning up deer bones on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking every second letter of MOOSESTAG, ignoring 'and', gives O, S, S, A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossa is the Latin plural of os, the anatomical word for a bone.

clue.text: Possibly Danish blue vessel that's used in kitchen?

parts.note: Danish blue is one kind of cheese, hence possibly
a cutter is a small sailing vessel

explanation.surface: A blue-painted Danish ship, wondering if it is a kitchen utensil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Danish blue' could be a colour of boat, but it is a blue-veined cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheese cutter is a kitchen tool, often a wire or blade, for slicing cheese.

clue.text: To make melodious, use less of a particular organ

definitions.meaning: first meaning: pleasant to listen to

definitions.text: use less of a particular organ
definitions.meaning: second meaning: to go easy on something is to use less of it, here the ear

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: going easy on one particular organ, the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Music that is pleasant to hear is described as easy on the ear, an idiom for tuneful.

clue.text: One might come down with this yellow flower, a sign of affection

definitions.text: One might come down with this

parts.note: yellow means cowardly, as does chicken
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Po is Italy's longest river
X is a kiss written at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A yellow bloom sent as a token of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is the crossword trick for a river, here the Italian Po. 'Come down with' means catch an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Chickenpox is an infectious childhood illness that a person may come down with, meaning catch.

clue.text: Large body of water developing leakage blocked by Nevil

indicators.note: blocked by means the shortened name sits inside the rearranged letters
developing means changing form, so the letters of leakage are rearranged

parts.note: Nev is the short form of the name Nevil

explanation.walkthrough: 'Developing' rearranges the letters of leakage into LAKEGEA, and the short form of Nevil goes in before the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Geneva is one of the largest lakes in Western Europe, on the Swiss-French border.

clue.text: It's a pain to pick up body hair

parts.note: to pick up a signal or sound is to hear it
tache is short for moustache, hair on the body

explanation.surface: Plucking body hair is painful.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'tache is British informal for a moustache; the blog notes it is facial rather than body hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartache is emotional anguish, a kind of pain.

clue.text: Ice ran out for the liqueur

indicators.note: for here means to produce, so the letters are reworked into the drink

parts.note: the nine letters that are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bar runs out of ice for the orange liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase 'Ice ran out' is the fodder; 'out' reads like an anagram signal but its letters are needed too, so the clue has no clean indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French orange-flavoured liqueur, a sweet alcoholic spirit.

clue.text: Each member of flock to finish meal?

parts.note: a tup is a ram, a member of a flock of sheep

explanation.surface: Every sheep in the flock is told to clear its plate.
explanation.walkthrough: Tup is a British dialect word for a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat up is to consume everything on the plate and so finish a meal.

clue.text: Made a fuss without getting at religious doctrine

indicators.note: without getting means losing the given letters

parts.note: created is British informal for made a fuss or complained
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who kicked up a fuss without having a go at a faith's teachings.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English to 'create' can mean to make a fuss, as in 'stop creating'.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a set of beliefs, especially the formal statement of a religion's faith.

clue.text: Exposed spouse-to-be in United ground

ground means crushed or milled, so the letters of United are rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'United ground' reads like a football stadium, but 'ground' is the anagram signal for United, giving INTUDE.

clue.text: Last-minute, disheartening hitch interrupts tour by cricket team

indicators.note: by means alongside, so the team stands beside the rest

parts.note: a cricket side has eleven players

indicators.note: interrupts means breaking into the middle of tour
disheartening removes the heart, leaving just the outside letters

parts.note: the word whose first and last letters are kept

explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartening' removes the middle of hitch, leaving its two outside letters; 'interrupts' puts them after the first letter of tour.

clue.text: Crime is discovered in the building

indicators.note: discovered in means is found inside the rearranged letters
building means constructing, so the letters of the are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

clue.text: Against hand lotion, in essence, repeatedly

parts.note: the word whose middle letters are taken
the word whose middle letters are taken

clue.text: Car entrepreneur to live somewhere Antipodean

parts.note: to be is to exist or live

clue.text: That's a relief map, at right-hand edge, showing fell

parts.note: the word whose final letter is taken
to fell a tree is to hew it

clue.text: Perhaps watch over function by church seeing what's paid

clue.text: Photograph crossbeam when it's separated?
